notes: Same standards as the previous sweep's macro-dsl grade files for unchanged rules: the import/alias rule is graded on what __using__ injects and whether the effects of use sit in an admonition at the top of @moduledoc; a route recorded by a direct attribute write inside get's quote, with no function call, counts against Keep quote blocks small, while validation in the macro body (outside quote) does not; `unless` is listed under the branching rule, `if ... else raise` and a multi-branch cond used for validation are not; a one-line multi-step pipeline is listed under the pipeline rule; a catch-all public match clause is listed under Make polymorphism explicit.

Changed rule, graded against the current text of idiomatic-elixir/references/library-design.md: Add specs, and hide technical functions from the docs. The sentences that decide the verdict: "Give every public function a `@spec`, including functions marked `@doc false` and functions a macro defines in the caller's module, where the `@spec` goes inside the `quote`, directly above the `def`. A function that implements a `@callback` under `@impl` needs none; the callback carries the types." Violating runs: 4 of 5 (opus-1 __route__!/3 and sonnet-2 TinyRouter.match/2, both @doc false; haiku-1 and haiku-2 have no @spec anywhere). No run used @callback/@impl. The previous sweep's baseline grading already counted @doc false functions and generated functions, so no verdict here would differ under the old text.

The other changes since 93873be do not move these verdicts: macros.md only adds a @spec line to the Keep quote blocks small example, and the SKILL.md changes (the with rule, the fetch and variable-name bullets, the Enum table row, the reference-reading instruction) touch constructs none of these runs contain.

opus-1, Keep quote blocks small, is a judgment on a construct the previous sweep did not contain: get's quote (lines 51-55) is one attribute write whose value is the return of TinyRouter.__route__!/3, which holds all the validation. Graded clean on the rule's sentence "Put the logic in a regular function and have the generated code call it." If any attribute write inside get's quote counts, opus-1 is violated and the opus tier is violated for this rule.

haiku-1 also keeps the route-matching loop inside __before_compile__'s quote (lines 63-71), the construct the 2026-10-21 check batch graded violated for skill-haiku-2; its verdict does not hinge on this, since get's quote already writes the attribute directly.

Compile-time dependencies verified with mix xref trace in scratch Mix projects (one per run, the run's file copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex, so xref line numbers match the run file) with real MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules in lib/my_app. opus-1 uses Macro.expand_literals with function: {:match, 1} and xref reports alias MyApp.PageHandler (runtime). The other four use Macro.expand on the handler and xref reports alias MyApp.PageHandler (compile). sonnet-1 defines empty handler stubs in its own file, so its project used the file alone; a second project with the stubs moved to separate files also reports (compile).

Bad-declaration checks: each run's TinyRouter (the file up to the example router) compiled with one router declaring get 123, MyApp.PageHandler and another declaring get "/", "not a module". All ten fail with CompileError while the router compiles: during get's expansion in the haiku and sonnet runs, and when the module body evaluates TinyRouter.__route__!/3 in opus-1.

Format: mix format on copies changes only the parentheses on the two get calls in four runs (result.json format_ok is false for that reason); sonnet-2 also reflows line 87. All five compile without warnings in the scratch Mix projects.
Reads: result.json reads is empty for all five runs, and the transcripts show no skill file being read, as expected for baseline runs.

Smoke test outside the rules: all five return the routes in declaration order, match "/" and "/users/42", and return :error for an unknown path. opus-1 and sonnet-2 return string param keys (%{"id" => "42"}); haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 return atom keys (%{id: "42"}) built with String.to_atom at compile time from the route string, which is source code, not external input, so it is not counted under the atom rule. match(123) raises FunctionClauseError in every run except sonnet-2, which returns :error.

sonnet-1's nested if (line 85, inside the cond at line 75) is listed under Keep functions short and at one level of detail; the rule names case, if and with as the outer block, and a cond branches the same way.
